stem: Farhan compares three counting plans for a large bag of marbles: the spoken list one, two, three, … ; a fixed list that stops at thirty; and a single chalk mark for each marble with no number words.

parts.text: Which claim correctly judges those plans for a large collection?

options.text: Call the answer the phrase unending sequence, and stop there.
The spoken list keeps going and stays usable; the list that stops at thirty is finite; chalk marks alone can continue but become cumbersome.
Prefer chalk marks because each mark is the largest printed symbol on the board.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A useful count needs an unending standard sequence that stays easy to use; stopping at thirty fails for larger bags, and bare marks grow too hard to read.

teacher.key_rationale: Usability needs both an unending sequence and a compact standard form. Naming the phrase alone, or picking chalk marks for size, miss that joint test.
